meta.tool: Chrome DevTools evaluate_script — rAF frame sampler driving continuous pan + zoom on /tree
meta.dataset: private family GEDCOM — 252-node descendants subtree (largest from rootId=1); 251 edges
meta.note: React Flow uses onlyRenderVisibleElements, so nodes were fit-view'd + zoomed out to force ALL 252 to mount (worst case) before sampling. Display refresh 144Hz (frame budget 6.9ms). Pan is a single GPU-composited viewport transform, so cost is ~independent of node count once mounted.

results.scenario: 4x CPU throttle (mid-tier mobile), all 252 nodes rendered

verdict: Not a bottleneck. Pan/zoom holds full display refresh with zero jank even with the whole subtree mounted under 4x CPU throttle. Re-check only against a root with thousands of simultaneously-visible nodes (this dataset's largest subtree is 252).
